audit_findings.title: The bridge may omit noncurrent marketable securities after removing their income
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,703.680 million, or $8.76 per diluted share; corrected values are approximately $106.68 bear, $139.82 base and $153.41 bull
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge excludes noncurrent marketable securities while owner earnings removes the portfolio interest income generated by them.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 27, 2025, we had approximately $4.1 billion of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error: June 2026 cash plus current securities equals the stated $2,666.190 million exactly, leaving the filed $1,703.680 million of noncurrent securities out. Adding them raises base value by 6.7% and the buy-below level from $91.74 to about $97.87. Even the corrected bull value remains about 45% below the $277.665 market price, so it does not change the present no-buy conclusion, although the published valuation should be corrected.
audit_findings.action: Add the June 27, 2026 noncurrent marketable securities at their filed $1,703.680 million fair value and rerun every scenario and the 30% margin-of-safety threshold.

audit_findings.title: Declared dividends may be an undeducted claim on bridge cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $607.651 million dividend payable, approximately $3.12 per diluted share; net valuation adjustment $0
audit_findings.mechanism: A dividend payable would reduce the cash bridge only if the payment belonged to holders separated from the shares represented by the valuation denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: The estimated payment amount for the dividend scheduled to be paid on March 27, 2026 was included in dividend payable on the Company’s consolidated balance sheets as of December 27, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 27, 2026 balance sheet already shows the prior $0.90 installment paid and a $607.651 million liability for the three remaining $1.05 installments. Their record dates—September 11 and December 11, 2026, and March 12, 2027—follow the September 5 valuation date. A purchaser of the valued shares on that date remains entitled to those distributions, so deducting the payable would remove $3.12 per share of cash without recognizing the matching shareholder benefit.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the September 5, 2026 ex-dividend status; absent an earlier ex-date, retain the payable without a separate bridge deduction.

audit_findings.title: Fiscal 2025 cash taxes may be temporarily favorable
audit_findings.magnitude: $33.643 million 2025 gap between $350.648 million tax expense and $317.005 million cash taxes paid; effect on the $1,377.6 million trend anchor unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If cash taxes or tax-related working-capital changes entered owner earnings without normalization, the 2025 result and fitted trend could include a temporary cash-tax benefit that reverses in 2026.
audit_findings.evidence: Due to the timing of tax payments, we expect net cash outlays for income taxes in fiscal 2026 to exceed income tax expense in fiscal 2026, and to increase as compared to fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates favorable 2025 payment timing and forecasts a 2026 reversal, but the supplied record does not show whether the owner-earnings calculation used tax expense, cash taxes, or normalized tax working capital. The filed 2025 timing gap is 2.2% of latest owner earnings, but its effect on the selected log-trend anchor and DCF cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Trace income-tax expense, taxes paid, deferred taxes and income-tax payable changes through every owner-earnings year; normalize timing differences and rerun the trend anchor and scenarios if cash-tax timing entered the series.

audit_findings.title: The growth cases may understate continuing Auto OEM capital drag
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 Auto OEM operating loss $48.634 million; first-half 2026 operating loss $3.565 million; prospective capital or restructuring drag unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Future Auto OEM facilities, development spending, contract-fulfillment investment or restructuring costs could reduce owner earnings or make the assumed 6% and 8% growth more capital-intensive.
audit_findings.evidence: Operating performance of the auto OEM segment has negatively impacted our consolidated operating income, as the associated revenue and gross profit have not been sufficient to cover these costs.
audit_findings.explanation: Historical consolidated owner earnings already includes reported Auto OEM operating costs and losses. The remaining concern is forward-looking. Performance improved materially in 2026, including $2.872 million of second-quarter operating income, but first-half results still showed a loss and do not establish that future growth can be funded without additional capital or restructuring costs.
audit_findings.action: Monitor segment operating profit, Auto OEM-related capital commitments, cost recoveries and restructuring disclosures; before the next rerun, separate maintenance and contract-required investment from growth investment.

audit_findings.title: Some bridged liquidity may not be freely transferable at face value
audit_findings.mechanism: Transfer approvals, withholding taxes or other repatriation friction could require a haircut to cash and securities included in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Non-trade related currency exchanges exceeding $50 million, or its equivalent, in a calendar year require approval of the CBC.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes a $50 million annual approval threshold for non-trade currency exchanges in Taiwan, but an approval requirement is not itself a demonstrated loss. The record does not identify how much of the $2,666.190 million bridge liquidity or omitted securities is held by Taiwanese entities, whether transfers are planned, or what tax or economic haircut would apply. Present materiality therefore cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain cash and securities by legal entity, jurisdiction and currency; document distributable reserves, CBC approval history and incremental repatriation taxes, then rerun the bridge using any evidenced realizable-value haircut.
